answer: Let lagoon, nectar, and juniper denote independently attested anchors. Trust propagates through the attestation graph by random walks of bounded length, limiting influence from distant or weakly connected nodes. A Sybil cluster joined to honest nodes by a sparse external cut has low conductance, so few walks cross into it; with capped per-identity weight, its aggregate voting influence is bounded by the cut capacity. Min-cut transitivity bounds prevent internal Sybil attestations from multiplying that influence without stronger external links.
